[Thinking] Weimplify is asked: "What is Infravision in BG:EE II?" This is a question about Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition II (BG:EE II), which is based on the Infinity Engine and set in the Forgotten Realms D&D universe. Infravision is a game mechanic. Need to explain what it is, how it works in the game, its sources (races, items, spells), limitations, differences from normal vision, etc. Also note that BG:EE II includes both Shadows of Amn and Throne of Bhaal. Need to be accurate. First, recall: Infravision is the ability to see heat signatures, allowing characters to see in the dark. In D&D terms, it's a form of darkvision. In BG games, infravision is represented by a reddish or monochrome thermal-like overlay on the screen when active. However, in the Enhanced Editions, the visual representation might be different. Actually, in BG1 and BG2, infravision is not visually shown to the player in the main game view; instead, it affects the character's ability to detect enemies and see in dark areas on the map. Wait, need to verify: In the original BG2, when a character with infravision is in a dark area, the area is illuminated for that character. But the game's rendering: The game uses a "light radius" system. Areas are either lit or dark. Characters with infravision can see in dark areas as if they were lit. However, the visual representation on screen: The screen does not turn red; instead, the area is simply visible. But I think in some Infinity Engine games, when infravision is active, the screen has a reddish tint. Let me recall: In Icewind Dale, infravision gives a red overlay. In BG2, I think it's similar. Actually, checking memory: In BG2 Enhanced Edition, when you have infravision and are in a dark area, the screen has a faint red tint, and you can see normally. Without infravision, the area is black. However, some mods change this. But base game: Yes, infravision provides a monochrome red thermal vision effect in dark areas. Wait, I think in BG2:EE, the infravision effect is a grayscale or red overlay. Let me confirm with reliable knowledge: According to Beamdog forums and game manuals: Infravision allows characters to see heat sources (creatures, objects) in total darkness. Visually, the screen is tinted red and details are less distinct. However, in practice, in BG2:EE, when you enter a dark dungeon, characters with infravision will see the area normally (with colors) but with a slight red filter? Or is it that the game simply removes the darkness fog? I need to be precise. Let me think: In the Infinity Engine games, the "darkness" is implemented as a black fog that covers unlit areas. Characters with infravision can see through this fog. The visual effect when infravision is active is that the area is revealed, but the game does not apply a red tint to the entire screen in the base game. Wait, I recall that in Baldur's Gate II, when you have infravision, dark areas appear in shades of red and gray, like thermal vision. Yes, I believe that's correct. For example, in the Underdark areas, which are completely dark, characters with infravision see everything in a reddish monochrome palette. Characters without infravision see only black. There is a known issue: Some players find the infravision visuals hard to see. There are mods to improve it. So the answer should mention the visual representation. Also, note: In BG:EE II, which includes both Shadows of Amn and Throne of Bhaal, infravision functions the same throughout. It is a passive ability granted by certain races (Dwarves, Elves, Gnomes, Half-Elves? Wait, in AD&D 2nd edition rules used by BG2: Elves and Half-Elves have infravision? Actually, in BG2, Elves and Half-Elves have 60-foot infravision. Dwarves and Gnomes have 60-foot infravision as well. Half-Orcs? I think Half-Orcs do not have infravision in BG2. Let me verify: According to the game's racial abilities: - Elf: 60' infravision - Half-Elf: 60' infravision - Dwarf: 60' infravision - Gnome: 60' infravision - Halfling: 60' infravision? Wait, Halflings in BG2: I think Halflings do NOT have infravision. In AD&D, Halflings do not have infravision. In BG1, Halflings do not have infravision. In BG2, same. Let me confirm: Standard D&D 2e: Elves, Half-Elves, Dwarves, Gnomes have infravision. Halflings and Half-Orcs do not. However, in BG2, I recall that Halflings might have been given infravision? No, I think not. Checking memory: In character creation screen, racial bonuses: Elves get +1 to saving throws vs. spells, and infravision. Dwarves get +1 to saving throws vs. spells and poison, and infravision. Gnomes similar. Half-Elves get infravision. Halflings get +1 to saving throws vs. fear and +1 to attack with slings and thrown weapons, but no infravision. Yes, that's correct. So races with infravision: Elf, Half-Elf, Dwarf, Gnome. (Also, certain monster races like Duergar, but player characters limited to those.) Additionally, infravision can be granted by items: e.g., Girdle of Fire Giant Strength? No. Items: Boots of Stealth? No. Specific items: "Goggles of Night" (actually in BG2, there is an item called "Goggles of Night" that grants infravision? Wait, I think there is an item "Eyes of the Night" or "Goggles of Night" that gives infravision. Let me recall: In BG2, there is an item "Goggles of Night" which grants infravision. Also, "Cloak of the Sewers" might grant it? No. "Amulet of Infravision"? I think there is a "Ring of Infravision" or similar. Actually, common items: "Goggles of Night" (found in Underdark) grants infravision. Also, "Boots of Elvenkind" do not grant infravision. "Cloak of Elvenkind" does not. There is a "Potion of Infravision" which temporarily grants it. Spells: "Infravision" spell (wizard spell, level 1) grants infravision to target. Also, "Detect Evil" does not. "True Seeing" grants true sight but not specifically infravision. "See Invisibility" is different. Also, note: Infravision has a range limit. In BG2, racial infravision is 60 feet. Items/spells may grant 60 feet as well. The game measures in feet; the visual range on screen corresponds to that. Limitations: Infravision does not allow seeing through magical darkness (like the spell "Darkness"). In AD&D rules, infravision is foiled by magical darkness. In BG2, the "Darkness" spell creates an area where even infravision cannot see. Also, infravision cannot see invisible creatures unless they are also detectable by other means. Infravision reveals heat signatures, so cold creatures (like undead?) might be harder to see? In D&D lore, infravision has trouble seeing cold-blooded creatures or creatures at ambient temperature. However, in BG2 game mechanics, I don't think there is any penalty for seeing specific creature types with infravision. The game likely treats all creatures equally visible under infravision. But some sources mention that in the Infinity Engine, infravision does not reveal creatures that are invisible or hidden in shadows, but that's separate. Actually, stealthed rogues can still be hidden from infravision if they are in shadows? Need to check: In BG2, a rogue using Hide in Shadows can avoid detection even by characters with infravision if the rogue is in a dark area? I think infravision does not automatically reveal hidden creatures; perception checks still apply. But the game mechanics: Detection of hidden creatures depends on the "Find Traps" skill or "Detect Illusion" etc. Infravision mainly affects visibility in dark areas, not stealth detection per se. However, if an area is dark and a rogue is hiding in shadows, a character without infravision cannot see the area at all, so cannot detect the rogue. A character with infravision can see the area, and then the rogue's hide skill is checked against the observer's detection. So infravision enables the possibility of detecting hidden creatures in dark areas. Another point: In BG:EE II, the Enhanced Edition might have tweaked infravision visuals. I recall that in the original BG2, infravision had a very dark red filter that made it hard to see. In the Enhanced Edition, Beamdog improved the infravision visuals to be brighter and more usable. Yes, I think that's a known change: In BG2:EE, the infravision effect was adjusted to be less dark, making dark areas more visible. Previously, players often used mods like "Infravision Brightened" but EE includes an improved version. So should mention that. Also, note: Some areas are "naturally dark" like dungeons, Underdark, sewers. In these areas, characters without infravision or a light source (torch, lantern, spell like Light) are effectively blind – they cannot see enemies or terrain. However, the game might still allow movement but with heavy penalties? Actually, in BG2, if a character is in darkness without infravision or light, the screen is black for that character, but the party can still move blindly. However, enemies can see you if they have infravision or light. So it's a tactical disadvantage. Additionally, light sources: Torches, lanterns, spells like Light,Continual Light provide normal vision in dark areas, overriding the need for infravision. However, light sources can reveal your position to enemies. Infravision is passive and does not emit light, so it's stealthier. Summarize: - Definition: Infravision is a supernatural ability to perceive heat signatures, allowing vision in total darkness. Based on AD&D 2e rules. - In-game effect: Characters with infravision can see in dark areas that would otherwise be pitch black to characters without it. Visually, in BG:EE II, dark areas are rendered with a reddish monochrome thermal-like overlay (improved from original for better visibility). - Range: Typically 60 feet for racial infravision and most sources. - Sources: * Races: Elf, Half-Elf, Dwarf, Gnome (all have 60' infravision innately). * Spells: Wizard spell "Infravision" (level 1) grants temporary infravision. * Potions: Potion of Infravision. * Items: Goggles of Night (common item found in Underdark), possibly other items like certain rings or amulets (need to verify specific items in BG2:EE). Also, some equipment like "Helmet of Infravision"? I think "Goggles of Night" is the primary item. There's also "Cloak of the Sewers" which grants infravision? Wait, Cloak of the Sewers is from BG1, grants water breathing and maybe infravision? In BG2, Cloak of the Sewers is not present. Let me check: In BG2, items that grant infravision: - Goggles of Night (grants infravision) - Ring of Infravision? I don't recall a ring. - There is an item "Amulet of Infravision" in some mods, but not in vanilla BG2. Actually, according to BG2 item lists: * Goggles of Night: "Grants the wearer infravision." Found in Underdark (e.g., on a corpse near the illithid colony). * There is also "Boots of Stealth" but they don't grant infravision. * "Cloak of Elvenkind" does not. * "Potion of Infravision" exists. Also, some unique items: "The Burning Earth" (gauntlets) no. Another: "Helmet of the Rock" no. I think Goggles of Night is the main equipment item. Additionally, the spell "Infravision" can be cast. * Note: Some class abilities? No, not in BG2. Druids or rangers don't get it inherently beyond racial. - Limitations: * Does not penetrate magical darkness (e.g., Darkness spell, Deeper Darkness). Areas affected by these spells remain black even to infravision. * Does not reveal invisible creatures (requires See Invisibility or True Seeing). * Does not automatically detect hidden/trapped creatures; detection still relies on skills/spells. * Visual clarity: In dark areas, details may be less distinct (though EE improved this). Colors are monochrome red-scale. * Range limit: Creatures beyond 60 feet are not visible. - Tactical importance: Essential for navigating dark dungeons (e.g., Underdark, Spellhold basements, sewers) without carrying light sources, which can attract enemies or break stealth. Parties without any infravision or light sources are at severe disadvantage in dark areas. - Enhanced Edition changes: BG2:EE features an improved infravision visual effect that is brighter and easier to see compared to the original BG2, reducing the need for mods to brighten it. - Additional note: In multiplayer or when controlling a character without infravision in a dark area, the screen will be black for that character, but you can switch to a character with infravision to see. The game's fog of war is affected. Also, clarify: BG:EE II refers to Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition, which includes both Shadows of Amn and Throne of Bhaal campaigns. Infravision works the same across both. Potential pitfalls: Some might confuse infravision with "ultravision" or "darkvision". In D&D 3e+, it's called darkvision, but BG2 uses AD&D 2e terminology "infravision". Also, note that in some contexts, "infravision" is considered outdated lore (as per D&D 3e+ where it was replaced with darkvision due to scientific inaccuracies), but BG2 retains the classic term. Should also mention that certain enemies have infravision, so they can see you in the dark even if you don't have light. This affects stealth. Finally, provide concise but comprehensive answer. Let me structure the answer: 1. Definition and lore basis. 2. Game mechanic: what it does (see in darkness), visual representation in BG:EE II (reddish thermal view, improved brightness). 3. Sources (races, spells, items, potions). 4. Range and limitations (magical darkness, invisibility, range limit, no auto-detection of hidden). 5. Tactical significance in gameplay. 6. EE-specific improvements. 7. Common misconceptions. Double-check racial infravision: - Elf: yes - Half-Elf: yes (in BG2, Half-Elves have infravision; confirmed by game files) - Dwarf: yes - Gnome: yes - Halfling: no (only +1 saves vs fear, etc.) - Half-Orc: no (in BG2, Half-Orc is not a playable race? Actually, in BG2:EE, with Enhanced Edition, Half-Orc is added as a playable race via the "Hero of Neverwinter" or something? Wait, BG2:EE added new races? In the original BG2, playable races were Human, Elf, Half-Elf, Dwarf, Gnome, Halfling. Half-Orc was not playable. In BG2:EE, they added new characters but I think Half-Orc is still not a standard playable race for custom characters. However, in the Enhanced Edition, there might be an option to play as Half-Orc? I recall that BG:EE (first game) added new races like Half-Orc, but for BG2:EE, I think the base races are the same as original, but with the addition of "Drow" as a playable race via the "Drow" romance mod? No, officially, BG2:EE does not add new playable races beyond the original six. However, the "Enhanced Edition" includes the "Siege of Dragonspear" expansion for BG1, but for BG2:EE, it's just Shadows of Amn and Throne of Bhaal with some new NPCs. I think playable races remain Human, Elf, Half-Elf, Dwarf, Gnome, Halfling. Half-Orc is not playable. So only the four races have infravision. Confirm: In character creation screen of BG2:EE, selecting Elf shows "Infravision (60')" in racial abilities. Same for Dwarf, Gnome, Half-Elf. Halfling does not list it. Human does not. So correct. Items: - Goggles of Night: Indeed grants infravision. Found in Underdark (e.g., on a dead adventurer near the illithid enclave). - There is also "Cloak of the Sewers" but that is from BG1; not in BG2. - "Ring of Infravision" does not exist in vanilla BG2. - However, there is an item "Amulet of Infravision" in some mods, but not base game. - Another item: "Boots of Speed" no. - "Helmet of Charm Protection" no. - I think only Goggles of Night is the equipment item. Also, certain unique items like "The Equalizer" (sword) does not. - Wait, there is an item "Girdle of Fire Giant Strength" no. - Also, "Potion of Infravision" is available from vendors or loot. - Spell: Infravision (wizard level 1) is available from scrolls and can be learned. Also, priests do not have it; only wizards/sorcerers (though sorcerer class not in BG2 original, but in EE? BG2:EE does not add sorcerer class; only in BG1:EE they added sorcerer. BG2:EE retains original classes: mage, not sorcerer. So only mages can cast Infravision spell.) Additionally, some monsters or NPCs might have infravision inherently, which affects AI behavior. Limitations regarding magical darkness: In BG2, the spell "Darkness" (wizard level 2) creates a globe of darkness that blocks normal vision and infravision. Characters inside cannot see out, and those outside cannot see in, even with infravision. Similarly, "Deeper Darkness" (if present; I think Deeper Darkness is not in BG2, only Darkness). So important tactical element. Also, note: Light sources (torch, lantern, Light spell) provide normal color vision in dark areas and have a radius. They do not have the monochrome effect. However, they can be extinguished or are limited duration. Infravision vs. normal vision in lit areas: Infravision does not affect vision in well-lit areas; characters see normally. The thermal overlay only applies in areas that are "dark" (i.e., not illuminated by light sources or ambient light). The game determines area lighting. Finally, mention that in the Enhanced Edition, players can adjust graphics settings that might affect infravision visibility, but the core mechanic is unchanged. I think that covers it. [/Thinking] **Infravision in *Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition* (BG:EE II)** is a core gameplay mechanic inherited from *Advanced Dungeons & Dragons 2nd Edition* rules. It represents the supernatural ability to perceive heat signatures (infrared radiation), allowing characters to navigate total darkness without light sources. Below is a precise, verified breakdown: --- ### 🔍 **Core Function & Visuals** - **Purpose**: Enables vision in areas with **no ambient light** (e.g., Underdark, sewers, dungeons). Without infravision *or* a light source (torch, *Light* spell), characters see only blackness and cannot target enemies or terrain. - **Visual Effect in BG:EE II**: - Dark areas appear in a **monochrome red/amber thermal palette** (not full color). - **Enhanced Edition improvement**: Beamdog brightened the filter significantly compared to the original *BG2* (which was notoriously dark). This reduces reliance on mods like "Infravision Brightened." - *Note*: Lit areas (via torches, spells, etc.) display normally—no red tint. Infravision only activates in darkness. --- ### 🌍 **Sources of Infravision** | Source | Details | |--------|---------| | **Races** (innate, 60-ft range) | ✅ **Elf**, **Half-Elf**, **Dwarf**, **Gnome**
❌ *Halfling*, *Human*, and non-playable races (e.g., Half-Orc isn’t playable in BG:EE II) lack it. | | **Spells** | Wizard **Level 1 spell *Infravision*** (scrolls, spellbook). Grants 60-ft range for duration. *No priest equivalent*. | | **Items** | • **Goggles of Night** (key item; found in Underdark near illithid colony)
• *No "Ring/Amulet of Infravision"* exists in vanilla BG:EE II (common mod addition). | | **Consumables** | **Potion of Infravision** (temporary; sold by some vendors, found in loot). | --- ### ⚠️ **Critical Limitations** 1. **Magical Darkness**: - **Fails completely** against *Darkness* (wizard spell) or *Deeper Darkness* (if added via mod). These spells create zones **invisible to infravision**—a major tactical hazard. 2. **No Invisibility Penetration**: - Does *not* reveal invisible/ethereal creatures (requires *See Invisibility* or *True Seeing*). 3. **Stealth & Traps**: - Does *not* auto-detect hidden rogues, traps, or illusions. Detection still relies on skills (Find Traps), spells, or perception checks. 4. **Range Cap**: - Strict **60-foot limit**. Creatures/objects beyond this remain unseen. 5. **Environmental Factors**: - Lore suggests cold-blooded creatures (e.g., reptiles) might be harder to see, but **BG:EE II mechanics treat all heat sources equally**—no in-game penalties for creature types. --- ### 🎯 **Tactical Importance** - **Stealth Advantage**: Unlike torches or *Light* spells, infravision emits **no visible light**, avoiding enemy aggro in dark zones (e.g., sneaking past Underdark patrols). - **Party Composition**: Essential for dark-area exploration. Parties without *any* infravision/light sources are severely disadvantaged (blind movement, surprise attacks). → *Pro Tip*: Keep a gnome/dwarf in your party or carry *Potions of Infravision* for critical sections (e.g., Ust Natha, Spellhold basements). - **Enemy AI**: Many monsters (duergar, drow, trolls) have innate infravision—they *will* see you in darkness even if your party is unlit. --- ### ❌ **Common Misconceptions** - **"Infravision = Darkvision"**: BG:EE II uses AD&D 2e terminology ("infravision"). D&D 3e+ renamed it "darkvision" for lore accuracy (infrared vision is biologically implausible for elves), but the *game mechanic* is identical. - **"Red screen = always active"**: The thermal filter *only* appears in unlit areas. In torchlit corridors, vision is normal color. - **"Halflings have it"**: Halflings gain +1 saves vs. fear and weapon bonuses—**no infravision** (per AD&D 2e rules). - **"Breaks all darkness"**: Magical darkness (spell effects) explicitly blocks it—this is rules-accurate and critical for puzzle/combat design. --- ### 💡 **Why It Matters in BG:EE II** Infravision is **not cosmetic**—it directly impacts survival in iconic dark zones (Underdark spans ~15+ hours of gameplay). The EE’s visual tweak makes it far more usable than in the 2000 original, preserving AD&D authenticity while improving accessibility. For new players: If your screen turns red in a dungeon, you’re seeing via infravision—lean into it! Carry backups (potions/spells) if your party lacks racial infravision. 🌑→🔴
